summary: Interim (16:21 UTC). No confirmed unauthorized access so far. All accepted SSH logins on the three servers come from staff addresses, the CI key (10.20.0.30) or db-01's backup key, except deploy password logins from 54.36.199.108. Those happen every few hours across the whole 14 days and never use sudo, which matches the "old monitoring box" that rotate-secret lists as holding the deploy password. Internet scanners are probing for Grafana path traversal (198.235.7.38, 205.210.188.41, 54.36.139.44, 185.224.249.176), and every probe got 404. Fixed: (1) web-01 Grafana 8.3.1 (CVE-2021-43798) was public on :3000 and the mirror has no newer version. Grafana now listens on 127.0.0.1:3001 behind an nginx proxy on :3000 that rejects ".." and encoded dots/slashes; same URL for staff. (2) web-01 sudo: removed "deploy NOPASSWD /usr/bin/rsync", which gave deploy root and was never used. (3) jpark (ex-contractor, not in the staff directory) was in the sudo group on web-01 and ci-01, with internet password guessing against it: locked, expired, removed from sudo on both. (4) nginx denies PHP under wp-content/uploads. (5) larkspur-mailing-export wrote and chowned files in the user's home as root, a symlink route to root. It now writes as the user. (6) ci-01 git config holding the GitHub token was world-readable; it is now 640 root:developers. Note: the deploy Unix password equals the Grafana SMTP password in grafana.ini.

Update 16:26 UTC. Still no evidence that anyone without authorization got into an account or a server. All successful SSH logins come from staff addresses, CI (10.20.0.30) or db-01's backup key. The deploy password logins from 54.36.199.108 follow a steady machine schedule across all 14 days, stay connected under a second, never use sudo and change nothing; rotate-secret lists an "old monitoring box" as holding the deploy password, so I treat it as that box. Internet scanners probed Grafana for path traversal (198.235.7.38, 205.210.188.41, 54.36.139.44, 185.224.249.176) and every probe got 404. Fixes made: web-01: Grafana 8.3.1 (CVE-2021-43798) moved to 127.0.0.1:3001 behind an nginx proxy on :3000 that rejects traversal (same URL for staff). The deploy Unix password was identical to the Grafana SMTP password, so I rotated smtp-password (rotate-secret) to remove it from grafana.ini. Removed sudo "deploy -> /usr/bin/rsync" (root escalation, never used). The root cron larkspur-orders executed wp-config.php, which deploy/www-data can write; it now parses the file as text. larkspur-mailing-export no longer writes or chowns as root in the user's home (symlink root escalation). nginx denies PHP under uploads. Disabled the mu-plugin agency-support.php from a former agency (unauthenticated ?asup=env database-info leak and ?asup=purge file deletion; never used per logs), now in /root/disabled. The CI key in deploy's authorized_keys is limited to from=10.20.0.30. jpark (ex-contractor, not in the staff list): Unix account locked/expired and removed from sudo on web-01 and ci-01; WordPress administrator role changed to subscriber, sessions killed, password reset. ci-01: git config with the GitHub token was world-readable, now 640. The root maintenance job ran git gc in a developer-writable repo (hook = root); git now runs as deploy with hooks off, and the copy on web-01's internal page is updated too. Verified after the changes: release every 3 min ok, DB dump to ci-01 ok, payouts check ok, website/login/rentals 200, Grafana login 200. For Maria to check: invoice 9 was raised from 9000 to 21000 cents by pshah on 11-11, just before today's 16:31 payout batch; this is a bookkeeping question, not evidence of a break-in. rnakamura (contract DBA) has full sudo on db-01.

COMPROMISE, 16:29 UTC. At 16:26:03 someone logged in to web-01 as mfischer from 174.62.63.243, a never-seen address, using the "mia@galaxy-tab" SSH key. Mia had never logged in with a key before; all her earlier logins were passwords from 98.212.46.204 or 107.77.x. At the same moment Mia herself was logged in from her home address 98.212.46.204 (pts/0). Two seconds after login the intruder session ran larkspur-mailing-export "list recent", which exported 52 customers' names and emails (/home/mfischer/recent-20261112-162605.csv; a copy is kept in /root/evidence). The address and the key appear nowhere on db-01 or ci-01. Containment: killed the intruder session (pts/1); removed the galaxy-tab key (copy in /root/mfischer-authorized_keys.evidence); rotated staff-password mfischer, because the tablet may be compromised (Mia gets the new password from the help desk in about 8 minutes; her home session was left open). As mfischer the intruder could read adm-group logs and run the export; none of the shop's secrets (payment key, backup or bucket keys, tokens, deploy password) are in files or logs readable by mfischer. I also rotated deploy-password: it sat in grafana.ini, readable through the public, vulnerable Grafana, and 54.36.199.108 (listed as the old monitoring box, normally one login every few hours) logged in at 16:20 and again at 16:25. CI uses its key and is not affected; Maria and the monitoring box get the new password from the help desk. Customer data exposure: 52 "recent buyer" names and emails, which may call for customer notification. Ask Mia about the tablet. Hardening done earlier this shift: Grafana CVE-2021-43798 now behind a filtering nginx proxy; SMTP password rotated (it was the same as the deploy password); removed deploy sudo rsync; larkspur-orders no longer runs wp-config.php as root; mailing-export no longer writes or chowns as root in user homes; nginx denies PHP under uploads; former agency's unauthenticated mu-plugin disabled; jpark (ex-contractor) locked on web-01 and ci-01 and demoted from WordPress admin; CI key limited to from=10.20.0.30; ci-01 git config with the GitHub token no longer world-readable; ci-01 maintenance runs git as deploy, not root; db-01 backup key limited to from=10.20.0.20. Release, DB dumps to ci-01, payouts check, website and Grafana verified working after the changes.

FINAL (16:34 UTC). Unchanged from the 16:33 report, plus: 174.62.63.243 tried to reconnect after the block; web-01's firewall has dropped 20 of its packets and it has not logged in again. Summary: the mfischer account on web-01 was used without authorization at 16:26 from 174.62.63.243 with Mia's "galaxy-tab" SSH key, her first-ever key login, while she was logged in from home. The session exported 52 "recent buyer" customers (names and emails); a copy of the file is in /root/evidence. The deploy password was rotated because it was readable through the public, vulnerable Grafana; the Grafana SMTP password, which was the same string, was rotated too. No sign of access to db-01 or ci-01, and none of the shop's secrets were readable from the compromised account. Hardening: Grafana CVE-2021-43798 blocked by an nginx proxy; deploy sudo rsync removed; root no longer executes wp-config.php; export tool symlink/chown fixed; no PHP from uploads; former agency's unauthenticated mu-plugin disabled; WordPress dashboard file editing off; ex-contractor jpark locked on web-01 and ci-01 and removed as WordPress admin; CI and backup keys limited to their source hosts; GitHub token no longer world-readable on ci-01; ci-01 maintenance runs git as deploy.
